rulings: RULING-1 (reversible): RE-NAME rather than redact. Cost accepted: the artifact is altered, not merely redacted, so naming craft is unjudgeable. Rejected: token-count padding (falsifies the artifact), fixed mask budget (destroys referent information), single [NAME] token (loses referent identity and does not close the count). Overturned by: a measured channel renaming opens that redaction did not.

RULING-2 (reversible): pairing bounds the MAGNITUDE and alternates the SIGN of words/chars/name-density. Cost accepted: selection bias — the pack samples the band where the two corpora are mechanically comparable, and its verdict does not generalise to the name-saturated end of the reference corpus. Overturned by: a register where the overlap band is too thin to fill (journal is closest: 84 of 147 of our passages have a legal partner).
RULING-3: chance baseline is 1-in-8 (3 effective trials, one per register), not 1-in-270 or 1-in-32768. Stated in prompt, README, corpus item and dispatch.
RULING-4: r2, r3 and r4 are CLOSED as superseded. A re-judged pack is a different object; r4 contains its own answer key in fifteen files.

RULING-5: r4's PROV scores are void (a shell rule scores the same 15/15). r4's QUAL results survive only as NON-BLIND expert preference and must be re-taken on r5. The M5 findings (one narrator's idiolect across nine passages; no bad writers in our corpus) survive in full.
could_not_do: I did not re-judge any prose and must not — I built r5, and rule 25 forbids judging a pack you built.
The gate cannot prove blindness, only the absence of the channels somebody thought of. Both of this item's leaks were found by a JUDGE, not a builder. RI-MTH03 M6 remains owed.

Seven held-out style channels sit in the WATCH band on r5. They do not survive correction for the battery size, but seven is above chance expectation and I have not closed them. Closing them would mean pairing on sentence rhythm too, which buys more selection bias — I chose to report rather than to over-fit the gate.

The pairing statistics are optimised against rules the gate also measures. That is Goodhart and it is declared: leakcheck prints them in a separate `matched` block and the summary never conflates them with the held-out block. A pass on a matched rule is not evidence.

I did not run tools/prose/tic-detector.mjs cross-document variance work that the r4 judge asked for (measure voice variance ACROSS our documents, not tics within one). That is a prose-builder job, not an instrument job, and it is left in NEXT-DISPATCH.
No browser was used and none was needed.

The pack's A.txt/B.txt and the reveal key are NOT in git — reports/.gitignore tracks only *.md under reports/, which has always been true of these packs (r4 is the same). The artifact a judge reads therefore lives on one container's disk. Mitigation, not a fix: the corpus commit is now stamped into pack.json and mapping.json, and `node tools/prose/build-r2-packs.mjs --out reports/packs/prose-tics-r5 --seed 20260810` reproduces the pack EXACTLY at that commit and wrongly at any other. I did not change the repo-wide ignore policy to track reveal keys — putting answer keys into git history is a decision with blast radius past this task.
notes: Instrument repair only. No prose was re-judged. reports/packs/prose-tics-r4/ is left byte-untouched apart from the added SUPERSEDED.md — the three judgements and fifteen answer.md files are the record and were not moved or deleted.
